text: In the main ending cutscene of Nightreign, a giant embodying the night awakens after an Erdtree petal touches it (resembling giants seen on Day 2 heading to the boss room on Day 3), is granted grace, looks toward the Lands Between, then turns away and walks into the dawn instead.

In the main ending, rather than the Night falling upon the Lands Between, grace is shown reaching out toward the Night, and the Nightfarers rise from the Round Table Hold as wisps of grace, freed at last.
The song that plays during the ending scene where grace reaches out to the Night is titled 'Dawn,' and thanks to the Nightfarers, the Night ends as though it never existed.

The Stability Ending results when three Nightfarers survive the three nights and defeat the third night's Night Lord, causing Limveld to settle into a quieter, temporarily peaceful state—its flickering sites of grace stabilizing and the landscape resembling its pre-catastrophe condition.
The Stability Ending is explicitly incomplete, as the forces represented by the Night Lords are not destroyed, only suppressed, persisting in Limveld's cosmological background.

The game presents three distinct endings (stability, remaining, and deeper understanding), each with its own emotional tone reflecting the true cost of the choice it represents, and Nightreign does not rank its endings or declare any single one correct.

After the stability ending, surviving Nightfarers either return to where they came from or remain in Limveld's relative peace; the meaning of staying differs depending on which character makes the choice.
If Wylder remains in Limveld, it may represent finding something worth staying for after a history of not finding anything worth staying for.
If Guardian remains in Limveld, it may represent committing to ongoing protection of a world that clearly needs it.
If Revenant remains in Limveld, it may represent accepting that who they are now matters more than whether they are continuous with who they were before death.

The ending of deeper understanding is the rarest, requiring sustained attentive engagement with the world across multiple expeditions; it occurs when Nightfarers not only defeat the third knight's Night Lord but demonstrate sufficient understanding of the forces that Night Lord represents, addressing the underlying cause rather than just its current manifestation, thereby altering Limveld's cosmological principles so future Night Lords differ and the world moves toward a new order rather than restoring the old one.
One ending represents the Nightfarers succeeding where the original civilization failed, finding a response to the Night Lords that the civilization's understanding could not produce.
Unlike the Duchess's story, Wilder's questline leads to an actual game ending.
After defeating the corrupted White Horn, the Raider returns his armor to him, freeing him from the Night's hold and allowing the Raider to reclaim his identity as the Black Claw.
After Heolstor's defeat, a different, possibly truer version of the Round Table is revealed.

The default ending action, used for any Nightfarer besides Wylder, is to take the primordial Night Lord's Great Rune and give it to an unidentified corpse seated at the Round Table, after which the chosen Nightfarer dissolves into yellow essence that circles the Round Table, implying a return to the Erdtree or their original world.
In the Recluse's ending, she finds her infant lying on the bed and cradles it lovingly, writing that 'the crying hath now ceased' as the child finds peaceful slumber.

In Iron Eye's ending, he kills the mysterious corpse with a knife, gaining freedom from the Round Table's fellowship, but the Night is stated to continue regardless, as 'the night is far from over' and never ceases.
In Wylder's ending, after killing the Night Lord, he inserts a Larval Tear into himself and collapses, while the Night Lord wanders off.
Wylder's action appears intended to save his sister, since the Night Lord's death would otherwise end the Round Table and the Priestess, his sister.
Wylder seemingly becomes a new Night Lord himself, prolonging his failing body and saving his sister, with his armor remaining unchanged, supporting the amalgamation theory of the Night Lord.
The ending implies the Nightfarers have restored the Lands Between to its original, undestroyed state, free of the Night's corruption.
